case.exact_velocity: u_x(y,t) = U0 sin(k y) exp(-nu k^2 t), k = pi/H
case.exact_energy: E_k(t) = E_k(0) exp(-2 nu k^2 t)
case.initial_condition: u_x = U0 sin(pi y / H), u_y = 0, no body force
case.boundaries: three layers of wall particles above and below the slab, wall_friction = 1 (no slip at both plates); the lateral ends are an open boundary and no metric is taken near them
case.integrator: explicit Euler, vel += dt*acc; pos += dt*vel, apply_boundary after each drift, Verlet pair cache

viscosity_control.description: half the viscosity must halve the decay rate

dt_control.description: half the time step must not change the rate

inviscid_without_walls.description: no viscosity, no walls: the pressure term alone is pairwise antisymmetric, so sum m u_x is invariant

viscous_without_walls.description: viscosity on, no walls: the m_j/rho_j weighting is antisymmetric only when rho_i = rho_j, so this is the momentum the viscous form does not conserve

with_walls.description: with rigid wall particles the reaction is discarded by design (the walls are static), so this drift is a boundary reaction, not a defect
